problem: Navigation training data is limited by scale: real scanned scenes (MP3D/HM3D) are few and costly, procedural simulators have sim-to-real gaps, and generative video models lack persistent 3D structure and collision geometry for closed-loop interaction.
motivation: Scaling data has driven progress in LLMs and vision models, but embodied navigation lacks scalable, high-fidelity, physically grounded interactive environments. Large collections of images and videos exist and could be turned into interactive scenes if geometry and appearance synthesis are handled separately.
key_idea: Decouple 3D spatial anchoring (feed-forward feature Gaussians from posed RGB-D) from photorealistic observation synthesis (a geometry-aware one-step MeanFlow pixel-flow renderer). Then build a fully automated data engine on top that produces about 10M navigation samples from about 20K scenes.
insight: Explicit 3D projection plus alpha-gated generative completion gives real-time panoramic RGB-D rendering that is more robust to sparse, noisy input than pure Gaussian splatting or pure generation. The ablation shows that removing the pixel flow drops PSNR from 20.15 to 17.75. Removing alpha-gated fusion, semantic features or self-distillation each also hurts. For navigation, data scale is the main driver. With the same architecture, SR on R2R-CE rises log-linearly from 46.1 (R2R/RxR only) to 66.3 with 10M Image2Sim samples and is still unsaturated. Training only in the neural sim transfers zero-shot to Habitat and to a real robot.
method: Feed-forward feature Gaussian encoder: a frozen DINOv3 ViT-L semantic stream plus a detail stream (RGB, depth, normals, rays) is decoded into dense 3D feature Gaussians. Centers are unprojected from depth, and the encoder handles both pinhole and panoramic cameras.
Alpha-gated source state: the splatted RGB-D prior is mixed with noise scaled by (1-alpha), so reliable regions stay near the projection and holes are left to generation.

One-step pixel-flow renderer: a UNet with an 8-layer transformer bottleneck, AdaLN time injection, SPADE-like semantic injection and alpha-gated skips. It is trained with pixel MeanFlow (JVP, opacity-weighted loss) and outputs 512x1024 panoramic RGB-D at about 40 FPS on an RTX 4090.

Momentum self-distillation: an EMA teacher conditioned on the GT RGB-D source supervises the student's multi-scale decoder features, plus LPIPS, reconstruction and DINOv3 alignment losses, in a 3-stage curriculum.

Motion simulation: voxelized navigable graph (Mask2Former floor segmentation, EDT clearance, GPU ray marching). Collision-aware Dijkstra planning, pure-pursuit control, wall sliding and stuck detection, using a Habitat-like discrete action space.

Data engine: YOLO-World object mining with IDF long-tail goal sampling, length-bucketed and furthest-point trajectory sampling, and Qwen3-VL-32B instruction annotation in R2R, REVERIE and Demand styles with built-in QA.

Image2Nav policy: Qwen3-VL-4B fine-tuned with 70K-step behavior cloning and 10K-step online DAgger in Image2Sim. It uses streaming sparse-dense context (24 history frames plus an 8-frame recent window).

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (fine-tuned LLM + MLP projector) for Image2Nav; Image2Sim renderer trained from scratch on top of frozen DINOv3
setting.training_data: R2R/RxR human data transferred into Image2Sim, plus up to 10M synthetic VLA samples from 19,936 scenes (RealSee3D, Structured3D, ARKitScenes, HM3D, ScanNet, Gibson, MP3D; 29 val/test MP3D scenes excluded). Instructions generated by Qwen3-VL-32B.
setting.observation: monocular RGB only (pinhole 336x336 at 90° FOV, or equirectangular 512x336 at 180° FOV) with history frames
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 15°, STOP (two actions predicted per step)
setting.simulator: Image2Sim neural simulator for training; evaluated zero-shot in Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE, REVERIE-CE)
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged GT source state is used only for the training-time distillation teacher)

numbers_note: Real-world results are counts out of 20 trials (Image2Nav path-follow OSR 14/20, SR 11/20; goal-oriented OSR 13/20, SR 9/20), and they are not included in the numbers list. Rendering-quality results (e.g. PSNR 17.43 and SSIM 0.470 on RealSee3D-Real, 45.6 FPS) are also not benchmark navigation numbers.
results: Image2Nav, trained only in Image2Sim and evaluated zero-shot in Habitat, reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 66.3 / SPL 61.5 (90° FOV) and SR 70.3 / SPL 65.6 (180° FOV). This beats the strongest baselines DualVLN (SR 64.3) and EfficientVLN (SR 64.2). It also leads on RxR-CE (SR 70.7) and REVERIE-CE (SR 53.7 vs D3D-VLP 47.5). In the real world it improves SR from 8/20 to 11/20 on path-following and from 5/20 to 9/20 on goal-oriented tasks over the strongest baselines.
limitations: The compact renderer trades generation capacity for real-time speed and still shows artifacts and hallucination under heavy occlusion.
The simulator only models navigation-level physics: no contact dynamics, movable objects or humans.
VLM-generated instructions may carry linguistic bias or semantic mismatch. The real-world evaluation is small (20 trials per setting).
